messages: Six months is right on time, and the green light is his body, not the calendar: sitting with support, steady head, watching your food and reaching for it. Week 1, once a day, offer a couple of teaspoons of a single soft food - iron-rich meat, egg, or an iron-fortified cereal, or a soft strip of vegetable he can hold. Pick a calm moment when he is alert, not overtired. Expect most of it to end up on his chin. That is normal - this first week is practice, not nutrition. Milk stays his main food.

Weeks 2-3, build to twice a day and widen the menu - one new food every couple of days so you can spot any reaction. This is also the window to offer the common allergens on purpose, not avoid them: smooth peanut butter thinned with water, well-cooked egg, dairy. A little in, watch, offer again. Expect gagging now and then - it is loud but it is the reflex working, and it is not choking. Always seated, always with you right there, never food in a propped bottle. His appetite will swing day to day - follow his cues, and stop when he turns away or shuts his mouth.

By week 4 you are aiming for three small meals alongside his milk, with real texture - lumps and soft finger foods, not only smooth purees, since getting texture in now makes it easier later. You will know it is working when he opens for the spoon, self-feeds bits, and shows steady interest. If he consistently refuses all solids by around 8 or 9 months, or if any food brings swelling, hives, or trouble breathing, that is one to raise with his doctor. His 6-month well-baby visit is a good time to check in on how it is going.
